title: Electric Field Induced Changes of a Diffusion Flame and Heat Transfer near an Impinging Surface
summary: Ground (1 g) study of a small diffusion flame impinging on a plate under an applied electric field, using an IR camera and schlieren imaging. The ion-driven wind substantially changes the heat-flux distribution on the plate, most when the plate is just above the flame tip. No microgravity data.

items.claim: Ground impinging-flame heat-transfer study; no ISS or microgravity data.
items.quote: The results show that electric fields affect substantially the heat flux distribution through the ion-driven wind, particularly when the plate location is just above the flame tip.

notes: Open access (MDPI, CC BY) but mdpi.com refused automated download (HTTP 403); abstract read via Semantic Scholar.

title: Electrical Aspects of Impinging Flames
summary: Y.-C. Chien's UC Irvine dissertation on electric-field control of flames impinging on surfaces (CO release and heat transfer), ground experiments only. CO escapes along the cold boundary layer on the fuel side; plate distance matters more than field strength.

items.claim: Ground dissertation on impinging flames; plate proximity dominates CO emission over field strength.
items.quote: In addition, the plate proximity to the flame has a stronger influence on the emission of toxic carbon monoxide than does the electric field strength.

notes: No DOI. Abstract from OpenAlex (eScholarship item 0ms7b11c); escholarship.org served a bot challenge, so the PDF was not read.

title: Modelling electric field driven convection in small combustion plasmas and surrounding gases
summary: Numerical model of the ion-wind (electric body force) flow around a small gaseous flame, treated as a unipolar two-fluid system; a toroidal vortex dominates the flow and space charge dominates the discharge. Background modelling, no microgravity data.

items.claim: Modelling of ion-driven convection around a small flame in 1 g; background to the E-FIELD physics.
items.quote: The results indicate a complex interaction between the combustion and current discharge environments where the flow field is dominated by the presence of a toroidal vortex structure and the discharge is dominated by space charge effects.

notes: Abstract from OpenAlex.

title: Canceling buoyancy of gaseous fuel flames in a gravitational environment using an ion-driven wind.
summary: Ground study using ion wind to cancel buoyancy locally around a capillary flame ('microbuoyant' condition). For methane the microbuoyant condition coincides with ion-current saturation; sooting fuels show hysteresis in the voltage-current characteristic. Precursor to E-FIELD.

items.claim: Microbuoyant condition for methane coincides with ion-current saturation (record finding on the gravity-mimicking basis).
items.quote: Furthermore, in this geometry, the microbuoyant condition for methane is found to coincide with ion current saturation when the capillary-to-plane distance is varied.

items.claim: Sooting fuels (C2Hx, propane) show hysteresis in the voltage-current characteristic: more soot, lower ion current at the same flow and potential; methane shows none.
items.quote: Soot generated in the C 2 H X and propane flames lead to a hysteresis in the VCC curve whereby increased sooting leads to lower ion currents at constant flow rates and applied potentials.

notes: Abstract from Crossref/OpenAlex. Ground (1 g) work; the hysteresis result is relevant to interpreting ISS ethylene ion currents but is not an ISS result, so it was not added to the record.

title: PLIF and chemiluminescence in a small laminar coflow methane-air diffusion flame at elevated pressures
summary: Ground study of OH PLIF and OH*/CH* chemiluminescence in a small laminar coflow methane-air flame up to 11.4 atm. With rising pressure the reaction zone thins at constant flame height and soot increases near the tip. No electric field and no microgravity; the only ACME link is that the same camera model flies on ACME.

items.claim: High-pressure 1 g diagnostics study; no E-FIELD or ISS data.
items.quote: The overall imaging results show that as the pressure rises there is a consistent thinning of the reaction zone while maintaining the same flame height, and there is an increasing concentration of soot near the flame tip.

items.claim: Link to ACME is only shared camera hardware.
items.quote: this camera model is also used on the International Space Station for imaging non-premixed flames as part of the ACME suite of microgravity experiments

notes: Author's final draft from the UPC repository (UPCommons). Funded by NSF and Keck; acknowledges the NASA ACME programme only for the loan of the camera.

title: Ion current and carbon monoxide release from an impinging methane/air coflow flame in an electric field
summary: Ground study of ion current and CO release from a methane coflow flame impinging on a plate under DC fields. Burner-to-plate distance dominates CO emission; ion current monitoring is proposed as a sensor of flame behaviour and CO release.

items.claim: Ground impinging-flame study; ion current proposed as an index of CO emission.
items.quote: The detailed findings indicate that a continuous monitor of ion current from the flame to the impinging surface can be an effective sensing index of flame behavior and CO emission.

notes: Green OA copy listed on eScholarship (qt0cp2j93g) but escholarship.org served a bot challenge (HTTP 202, empty); abstract read via Semantic Scholar.

title: Non-premixed axisymmetric flames driven by ion currents
summary: Ground coflow-burner study of positive DC fields: flame-base changes depend on burner geometry, CH* and chemi-ion production rise, a Roper-type model with an ion-wind term predicts the shape change, and the derived body force is 200-400 'N/m2'. Basis of the record's force-size comparison.

items.claim: Derived electrical body force 200-400 (stated N/m2), used in the record's force comparison.
items.quote: The calculated body force (200–400 N/m2) agreed well with the theoretical model.

items.claim: In the plane-to-plane (coflow-mesh) configuration the peak ion current density sits 2.5 mm off axis, unlike point-to-plane configurations where it stays on the centreline.
items.quote: The probe measurements also revealed that for the coflow geometry the peak current density develops 2.5 mm from the center axis.

notes: Abstract from Semantic Scholar. Ground work; the off-axis current density is background for ISS geometry, not added to the record.

title: Electric-field effects on methane coflow flames aboard the international space station (ISS): ACME E-FIELD flames
summary: The E-FIELD foundation paper: methods, ACME insert capabilities, procedures and first results for methane coflow flames in a ramping field on the ISS (tests March-November 2018). The flame is most compact at saturation and the voltage-current curve is parabolic after saturation, unlike 1 g.

items.claim: Most compact flame at saturation; parabolic VCC after saturation, unlike 1 g.
items.quote: The results show that the flame is most compact at saturation while the measured voltage-current characteristic (VCC) curve demonstrates parabolic behavior after saturation which differs from observations in 1 g on Earth.

items.claim: On-orbit tests ran March-November 2018, matching the PSI table dates.
items.quote: The on-orbit tests began in March 2018 using the modular ACME hardware within the ISS’ Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) and were completed in the same year November.
